title: No-Show Visits under CareLine Service Plans
content:
A visit where nobody gives the technician access within the wait time is a no-show. Under CareLine Service Plans the no-shows of a plan year up to the plan's free count carry no fee, and each later one carries the plan's no-show fee on the visit date. A no-show never uses a tune-up or a free trip.

The wait time, the free count and the no-show fee are the figures the product schedules set for the plan's tier.

### Care team questions and answers

**What makes a visit a no-show?**
Nobody giving the technician access within the wait time. A visit where access is given within the wait time is not a no-show.

**Which no-shows are counted against the free count?**
The no-show visits of the same plan year, counted up to and including the visit in question. Plan years run from the anniversary of the enrolled date, so the count starts again in each plan year.

**When is the fee charged?**
On the visit date of the no-show that carries it.

**Does a no-show use up one of the plan's tune-ups?**
No. A no-show never uses a tune-up.

**Does a no-show use up one of the plan's free trips?**
No. A no-show never uses a free trip.

### Counting through a plan year (hypothetical plan with a free count of 1)

| No-show visit of the plan year | Within the free count? | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| First | Yes | None |
| Second | No | The plan's no-show fee, on that visit date |
| Third | No | The plan's no-show fee, on that visit date |

For a hypothetical plan with a free count of 0, the first no-show of the plan year already carries the no-show fee.

A no-show in the next plan year is the first of that plan year.
